title: Road works insurance: a contractor's preparation checklist

seo.description: Prepare a road-project insurance file: sections, stages, contract requirements, machinery, traffic, neighbours, weather, handover and performance guarantees.
seo.keywords: road works insurance Moldova, road construction insurance, road contractor risks, infrastructure insurance preparation

content:
A road project needs assessment according to the phase of work, location and parties' responsibilities. Construction insurance, the contractor's machinery, third-party claims and a performance guarantee are different questions. Do not assume one policy title resolves them all.

Describe each section and its interface with traffic

For a quotation, prepare the site plan, section lengths, construction stages and arrangements separating works from public circulation. A new site and rehabilitation of an operating road have different contexts. Include bridges, culverts, existing networks and temporary works in the description, without assuming they are automatically insured.

  • Who is the client and who performs each category of work?
  • What is the contract value and which assets belong to the client?
  • Which machinery, stores and shipments need separate discussion?
  • When does each stage begin, pause and reach acceptance?
  • Which neighbouring property, utilities and access routes may be affected?

Turn contractual requirements into a verifiable list

Extract the contract's insurance requirements and ask how they correspond with the proposal: insured persons, periods, limits and exclusions. If the client requests a certificate, compare it with the full policy documents. Do not use a certificate to assume clauses absent from the contract. Identify the wording supporting each response rather than relying on a document's title.

Keep a change register as work advances

Use a table recording the section, change, date and reference document. Separate a quantity change from a different method or schedule. For each change, record whether it was submitted for insurance assessment and what reply was received. Do not confuse the client's technical approval with a policy amendment: the documents have different purposes.

At project meetings, review unconfirmed points and who must resolve them. If new machinery arrives or temporary storage is added, update the records even when the works value is unchanged. A short current list is more useful than a long initial presentation that no longer describes the site. It supports communication without confirming protection for any item.

A road site changes during construction

The insurance description should follow the actual stages: preparation, earthworks, networks, foundation, surfacing and acceptance, where these belong to the project. One section may combine new work with public circulation. Show which area is under construction, which remains in use and who organizes it. One address and contract value cannot adequately describe those arrangements.

For rehabilitation, distinguish the existing road from newly executed work. Record junction interventions, access to neighbouring properties and work near networks. This information supports assessment but does not establish that every object will be included. Request confirmation of the objects and periods in the documents proposed for the actual Moldovan project.

The section sheet: useful information before quotation

Give each section a code and use it in the schedule, budget and site-organization plan. Show any stages with separate acceptance. Questions about protection starting and ending are easier to clarify when stages have verifiable milestones. Do not present an estimated date as a confirmed contractual deadline.

  • Location and length of the section under consideration.
  • New construction, rehabilitation or a targeted intervention.
  • Value and main budget categories.
  • Existing structures and utilities nearby.
  • Stages, planned pauses and traffic-opening dates.
  • Contractors, subcontractors and the client's roles.

Do not publish sensitive technical plans or machinery-security details in the article or comments. Agree the transmission channel and document version for the actual file. After a project change, prepare a list of amendments rather than sending only a new archive with no explanation. For example, the same section code can connect the changed estimate with its revised schedule.

Works, machinery and transported goods need separate discussion

A paver, a road roller and material incorporated into the works are different objects. For each machine, identify the owner, place of use and any hire agreement. Separate mobile equipment, temporary installations and completed work. Naming the contractor as insured does not automatically include everything brought by that contractor or its subcontractors.

Transporting materials to the site can require a different assessment from storing and using them after arrival. Record who assumes risk in commercial agreements and which transport documents exist. Do not automatically assign site insurance the role of CARGO cover. The list separates questions; it does not confirm a universal package.

Traffic and neighbours: describe contact with other people

Pedestrians, residents, commercial vehicles or the client's traffic may continue using a road under construction. Describe the approved organization and who manages it. For possible third-party claims, ask which subject, limit and exclusions are proposed. Physical protection of the works does not demonstrate inclusion of every loss occurring nearby.

Identify known buildings, fences, access routes and networks in the surroundings. Use project documents and technical checks rather than assumptions from a public map. Put an unidentified utility or omitted object on the clarification list. This article gives no traffic-management instructions and does not replace technical or legal safety measures.

Weather and seasonal pauses need more than a policy label

For discussion, identify vulnerable stages and work left exposed during a pause. Ask how precipitation, accumulated water and other relevant phenomena are treated under the proposed conditions. Do not infer that every weather event is covered, or that a site photograph replaces the requested technical information.

If a seasonal pause is planned, describe its estimated duration and the measures included in the site arrangements. Check whether and how suspension and resumption must be declared. Extending the works contract does not automatically extend the policy. Request confirmation before the relevant period, using the procedure in the insurance contract.

A performance guarantee has a distinct file

The client may request a contractual guarantee and insurance documents for the work. Keep two headings in the file. One identifies risks and property assessed under the policy; the other identifies the guarantee requirement, accepted form and eligible issuer. Do not combine them by changing a certificate's title. Ask a specialist to review guarantee admissibility against the documentation and applicable framework.

For subcontracted work, extract each party's obligations. Check the policy's list of persons and how subcontractor activity is treated. A construction-contract clause does not automatically become an insurance clause. Where requirements differ, request an explanation before the relevant stage begins. Keep the original requirement beside the answer so the comparison can be checked later.

Illustrative change: a culvert added during rehabilitation

In an illustrative project, the initial design is supplemented with work on a culvert. The responsible person checks the estimate, schedule, method and affected existing property. Changing only the total value is insufficient. Present the additional work for insurance analysis and request confirmation of applicable conditions. This example describes no real policy or project.

Keep the amendment and the date from which the parties accept the change. If work begins before insurance clarification, do not state that later acceptance automatically protects an earlier period. Track the final documents and ask for any interval or object still unconfirmed to be identified. A conditional response should retain that status in the project file.

After an incident: document facts without exposing people

People's safety and appropriate intervention take priority. Follow project and insurance-contract procedures. Where safe, preserve the section reference, stage, observed conditions and affected work. Do not turn the initial description into a final conclusion about cause or responsibility before competent checks. Documentary work must not require entering an unsafe area for photographs.

Separate damaged assets, urgent measures and reinstatement work. Keep supply documents, work statements and expense evidence. Ask about inspection and approval of interventions while respecting safety. A repair invoice alone does not show that its amount will be compensated: assessment depends on the contract and actual circumstances.

Staged acceptance and transition to operation

Part of a road may be accepted or opened to traffic before the whole project ends. Prepare the documents and ask how that affects insurance. Do not give every section the same status automatically. Keep section-level records that both the technical lead and policy administrator can follow.

At completion, check which risks relate to execution, which duties continue and what assessment is needed for operation. Do not reuse site conditions as proof of protection at every stage. A useful contractor comparison includes confirmed documents, periods and limits alongside exclusions and unresolved points. Record differences explicitly rather than assuming a single project heading answers every stage.

Frequently asked questions about road works

Does site insurance remain unchanged after opening?

Ask for the distinction between execution, any subsequent periods and operation. Acceptance must be considered against the actual policy terms.

Is damage to underground networks included?

Describe known networks and ask about specific conditions. Do not infer protection merely because general liability is included.

Where should the discussion start?

With the contract, budget, schedule and site-organization plan. Legal clauses and procurement requirements also need specialist review.

Next step

Request a conversation with ING Broker to check assessment and intermediation possibilities. The broker explains options; risk acceptance, conditions and claims handling belong to the insurer under the contract. This material does not confirm product availability or coverage of a particular case.
